Hi,

i found a thread, in which Tom Hopper is creating a 'heatmap' on a
world map and i am heavily using his code to create basically the same
map (http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/
3c769e24dabc78db/c0fac63a3e0cba59?#c0fac63a3e0cba59).

my code including data, which is not fully cleaned up yet:
https://gist.github.com/833906
the map data is taken from the thread, direct link to the data:
http://www.box.net/tomhopper/1/22918943/452150764

the problem now is the coloring. if i execute the code from the gist,
i get this result:
http://bit.ly/gCj56X (image shack link to a jpg)

I also tried a gradient fill via scale_fill_gradient

p = p +
scale_fill_gradient(limits=c(0,1500000),low="red",high="white")

now my output is different, but not what i am after either and i get a
warning: "Categorical variable automatically converted to continuous":
http://bit.ly/g5oQdF (image shack link to a jpg)

I don't even know where the problem is located. Is it a map problem,
my code is generally wrong, do i read the data wrong?

Any help is appreciated.

Thomas

messages.author: 4c2460918214ec91
messages.subject: Re: geom_polygon on top of a map
parts:
Hi thomas-

One pleasant thing would be to include all your library calls at the top. I had discover that I had to install several libraries in an iterative manner....

the wc.txt file you supplied, and which I renamed world_counted.txt, has errors (extra comma in country names) on 3 lines 196,205,228. These cause errors in world.ggmape$y2007 which you could have discovered by
str(world.ggmape) and wondering why y2007 is a factor with a first level even shown of "deomocratic...." then you could have done a table(world.ggmape$y2007) to get perhaps a more clear view of what happened. next you might have printed elect.gen.tot to see the issues there. just some suggestions on how to trouble shoot this.

because y2007 was interpreted as a factor due to inclusion of , you have 112 levels in the color legend in your first plot. note how they were sorted too. when you convert factors to continuous you only get the factor index which in this case is less than 112, why everything looks like 0 in that scale range. you have to convert factors to numeric via numeric=as.numeric(as.character(factor)).

anyway, fixing the input file, you get a variable that is properly typed as integer and a map which is colored showing basically the US, phillipines, and west germany as having more y2007 than almost all other regions with the US way higher than these others. So, I think I'm getting your desired output. Just run your original example after fixing the input file.

Cheers,
James

parts:
Hi Tom-

(i had to install maptools, sp and gpclib which were required and I didnt have on my local system)

look at 

?cut

probably you'll do something like

world.ggmape$y2007.orig <- world.ggmape$y2007
world.ggmape$y2007 <- cut(world.ggmape$y2007.orig, c(0,5000,25000,50000,what you want here), include.lowest=TRUE)

then you could use the same code. It will use scale_fill_hue by default, which is usually nice. scale_fill_brewer is something i'd look at too for discrete/factor coloring.

James
